Context/Background:
Intraductal papillary neoplasms (IPNs),  including intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (IPMNs), intraductal oncocytic papillary neoplasms (IOPNs), and intraductal tubulopapillary neoplasms (ITPNs), are clinically detectable macroscopic non-invasive cyst-forming lesions, some of which progress to invasive pancreatic cancer. Proteins and glycoproteins have proven to be useful clinical biomarkers for classifying cyst-forming neoplasms in the pancreas.Here, we used proteomics and glycoproteomics to characterize a series of histologically and genetically well-characterized surgically resected IPNs, including IPMNs and IOPNs.

Our analysis included 69 IPNs (64 IPMNs and 5 IOPNs), 76 macro-dissected grossly normal duct tissues (NDs, with 32 of the 76 NDs coming from the same resection specimens as the IPNs), and 32 cyst fluid samples (22 from matched IPMN patients, 3 matched IOPN patients, 2 from unrelated IPMN patients, and 5 other cysts).
Prompt: Look at the list of glycoproteins upregulated in IPMNS with both KRAS and GNAS mutations compared to wild-type IPMNs and explain the pattern with activities of signaling pathways.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
In surgically resected intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (IPMNs), the subset harboring both KRAS and GNAS activating mutations was compared to wild-type IPMNs by glycoproteomic profiling (Wang et al. S3I). Samples: 64 IPMNs (genotyped for KRAS/GNAS), macro-dissected ductal epithelium. Assay: site-specific N-glycopeptide quantitation (log2FC, FDR). Definitive signal: 82 glycopeptide sites on 57 proteins were significantly upregulated (log2FC > 1, FDR < 0.05) in KRAS/GNAS-mutant vs WT IPMNs, including multiple glycosyltransferases, mucins, receptor tyrosine kinases, adhesion molecules, proteases, and signaling adaptors.  

Keywords  
• KRAS/GNAS mutations  
• O-linked glycosylation  
• Mucin biosynthesis  
• MET/ErbB signaling  
• Notch processing  

Candidate Genes  
MUC5AC, GALNT3, C1GALT1C1, ADAM10, MET  

Pathway Enrichments  

Overall enrichment ratios (Reactome_Pathways_2024): up 4, down 0 (100% upregulated terms; ratio ∞).  

KEGG_2016 (UP):  
| Theme                                    | Direction | Leading Genes                           |
|------------------------------------------|-----------|------------------------------------------|
| Mucin type O-Glycan biosynthesis hsa00512 | Up        | ST6GALNAC1; C1GALT1C1; GALNT5; GALNT3; GCNT1 |

Reactome_Pathways_2024 (UP):  
| Theme                                                | Direction | Leading Genes                               |
|------------------------------------------------------|-----------|----------------------------------------------|
| Chk1/Chk2-Mediated Inactivation of Cyclin B–Cdk1     | Up        | SFN; YWHAH                                   |
| O-linked Glycosylation of Mucins                     | Up        | GALNT5; C1GALT1C1; GALNT3; GCNT1; MUC5AC      |
| Activation of BAD and Translocation to Mitochondria  | Up        | SFN; YWHAH                                   |
| MET Interacts With TNS Proteins                      | Up        | MET                                          |
| GRB7 Events in ERBB2 Signaling                       | Up        | ERBB3                                        |
| MET Activates PTPN11                                 | Up        | MET                                          |
| Defective GALNT3 Causes HFTC                         | Up        | GALNT3; MUC5AC                               |
| SARS-CoV-2 Targets Host Intracellular Signalling…    | Up        | SFN; YWHAH                                   |
| Defective C1GALT1C1 Causes TNPS                      | Up        | C1GALT1C1; MUC5AC                            |
| O-linked Glycosylation                               | Up        | GALNT5; C1GALT1C1; GALNT3; GCNT1; MUC5AC      |
| Sema4D-Mediated Inhibition of Cell Attachment…       | Up        | MET                                          |

MSigDB_Hallmark_2020 (UP, ORA):  
| Theme               | Direction | Leading Genes                           |
|---------------------|-----------|------------------------------------------|
| KRAS Signaling Up   | Up        | TSPAN13; GALNT3; TLR8                   |

Analysis  
Across all libraries, glycosylation pathways dominate: core mucin-type O-glycan biosynthesis (KEGG) and O-linked mucin glycosylation (Reactome) exhibit the strongest enrichment (adjusted p ≤ 1.6 × 10⁻⁶ and 2.2 × 10⁻⁴, respectively). Key glycosyltransferases (GALNT3, GALNT5, C1GALT1C1, GCNT1) and mucin MUC5AC drive these signals, consistent with KRAS/GNAS-driven mucin overproduction. Simultaneously, oncogenic signaling modules are activated: MET and ERBB3 pathways (PI3K–AKT, PTPN11 engagement), Notch processing (ADAM10-mediated), and KRAS hallmarks. Cell-cycle checkpoint (Chk1/Chk2–Cdk1) and apoptosis (BAD) nodes also emerge, hinting at broader cell-cycle perturbations.  

Targeted (keyword-guided) subset  
Filtering ORA/GSEA by “glycosylation”, “Notch”, and “KRAS” yielded:  
| Term                                     | Direction | Adjusted P-value | Leading Genes                          |
|------------------------------------------|-----------|------------------|-----------------------------------------|
| Mucin type O-Glycan biosynthesis hsa00512 | Up        | 1.6 × 10⁻⁶      | ST6GALNAC1; C1GALT1C1; GALNT5; GALNT3; GCNT1 |
| O-linked Glycosylation of Mucins         | Up        | 2.2 × 10⁻⁴      | GALNT5; C1GALT1C1; GALNT3; GCNT1; MUC5AC |
| Constitutive Signaling by NOTCH1…        | Up        | 0.097            | ADAM10                                  |
| KRAS Signaling Up                        | Up        | 0.088            | TSPAN13; GALNT3; TLR8                  |

Key Genes/Proteins (Leading edge)  

Upregulated  
| Gene        | Direction | Role/Function                                         | Pathway(s)                                   |
|-------------|-----------|-------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| MUC5AC      | Up        | Secreted gel-forming mucin, ECM constituent           | O-linked glycosylation; mucin O-glycan biosynthesis |
| GALNT3      | Up        | Golgi polypeptide N-acetylgalactosaminyltransferase 3 | Initiation of mucin O-glycosylation           |
| C1GALT1C1   | Up        | Core-1 β1,3-galactosyltransferase chaperone           | Core-1 O-glycan synthesis                     |
| ADAM10      | Up        | Metalloprotease, Notch receptor S2 cleavage           | Notch receptor activation                     |
| MET         | Up        | Receptor tyrosine kinase                              | MET signaling (PI3K/AKT; PTPN11 activation)   |
| SFN (14-3-3σ)| Up       | Checkpoint adaptor                                   | Chk1/Chk2-Cdk1 inactivation; apoptosis (BAD)   |

Downregulated  
| Gene | Direction | Role/Function | Pathway(s) |
|------|-----------|---------------|------------|
| Not observed (no downregulated terms passed significance thresholds)                   |

Comparisons & Confidence  
• Glycosylation pathways are robustly shared between glycoproteomic signals here and prior IPMN transcriptomic studies (PMCID: PMC3912139).  
• Proteomic-only hits (e.g., ITGA6, EPHA2) flag adhesion/RTK remodeling, warranting cross-validation.  
• Single-modality signals (e.g., TMEM63A) remain lower confidence until orthogonal validation.  

Implications  
The coordinated activation of mucin O-glycan biosynthesis aligns with KRAS/GNAS-driven mucin hypersecretion in IPMNs, while concurrently upregulating MET/ErbB and Notch signaling—pathways implicated in progression to invasive carcinoma. These findings suggest that targeting glycosylation enzymes (e.g., GALNT3 inhibitors) or RTK/Notch axis (MET, ADAM10) could modulate both mucin deposition and aberrant signaling in mutant IPMNs.

Next Steps & Clarification  
1. Validate site-specific glycosylation changes by targeted glycopeptide MS and confirm enzyme activity (GALNT3, C1GALT1C1).  
2. Assess functional effects of ADAM10-mediated Notch activation in KRAS/GNAS-mutant IPMN organoids.  
3. Test MET inhibition on glycoprotein secretion and signaling cross-talk in mutant IPMN models.  
4. Clarify presence/absence of cell-cycle checkpoint (Chk1/Chk2) and apoptosis (BAD) activity by phospho-marker immunoblotting.  

References  
1. PMID: PMC10891078  Predictive potentials of glycosylation-related genes in glioma prognosis and their correlation with immune infiltration.  
2. PMID: PMC3912139   A GNAS Mutation Found in Pancreatic IPMNs Induces Upregulation of Mucin Genes.  
3. PMID: PMC10134423  Emerging role of non-invasive and liquid biopsy biomarkers in pancreatic cancer.
